headline_findings.title: Auth Diversity: Bearer Tokens & OAuth2 Dominate (77% & 51%)
headline_findings.summary: Bearer authentication (scoped personal access tokens, private apps) is the most widespread pattern (77 apps), followed by OAuth 2.0 (51 apps). API keys remain widely supported (38 apps) across developer-first platforms, though modern ecosystems increasingly favor scoped tokens with granular permissions.

headline_findings.title: 65% Self-Serve Velocity vs 35% Gated/Enterprise
headline_findings.summary: 65 out of 100 apps allow developers to acquire sandbox or production credentials with self-serve signup (42 free tier, 23 trials). 35% require paid commercial plans, manual developer review (e.g. Google/Meta Ads), or sales contact.

headline_findings.title: Category Gating Disparities
headline_findings.summary: Developer Tools (100% self-serve) and Productivity (90% self-serve) offer the lowest time-to-first-token. In contrast, Finance (50% gated) and Marketing/Ads (40% gated by compliance review) require high-touch human operations.

headline_findings.title: MCP Ecosystem: 14% Official, 41% Missing White Space
headline_findings.summary: 14 apps have official MCP servers (GitHub, Stripe, Notion, Linear, Jira, Sentry, Cloudflare, Supabase, Vercel, Shopify, Firecrawl, Devin, Slack, MongoDB). 45% have community implementations, while 41% have zero MCP coverage, offering clear white space for first-party Composio toolkits.

headline_findings.title: The Three Integration Traps: CLIs, Ghost APIs & Approval Walls
headline_findings.summary: Not all software tools are cloud REST APIs. Sherlock and Mermaid CLI are local command-line tools requiring shell subagents. fanbasis and Consensus lack public 3rd-party REST APIs. Google Ads and Amazon SP-API require strict developer credential vetting.
